obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the customer (covered entity)
trigger: Breach of security of a system the company maintains for a customer: unauthorized access of data in electronic form containing personal information (501.171(1)(a)), for example shopper logins, card data typed into a skimmed checkout page, or Social Security and driver license numbers in a mailbox
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, but no later than 10 days following the determination of the breach or reason to believe the breach occurred
notify: Each affected customer's security contact (the covered entity), with all the information the customer needs to give its own notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the company is a third-party agent for customer data on hosted sites and in hosted mailboxes (501.171(1)(h)). This is the company's main legal clock in the P08 incident

obligation: Customer's own notices (context; the customer's duty)
trigger: The customer receives the third-party agent notice and determines a breach of its data
deadline: Individuals and, if 500 or more Florida individuals are affected, the Department of Legal Affairs: no later than 30 days after the customer's determination
notify: The customer's affected individuals (shoppers, tenants, clients); the Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: No - the customer's duty. The company may send these notices on the customer's behalf if asked, but a failure is treated as the customer's violation (501.171(6)(b)). The company's facts sheet must reach the customer early enough for its 30-day clock

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals (company's own data)
trigger: Breach of personal information the company itself holds as a covered entity: about 190 customer portal sign-ins (email and password) and billing contacts of Florida residents
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (law enforcement delay under 501.171(4)(b); documented no-harm determination under 501.171(4)(c), kept 5 years and sent to the department within 30 days)
notify: Affected Florida residents, by mail or email
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the attacker also reached the customer portal (SYS-01)

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (company's own data)
trigger: Breach of the company's own personal information affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely - the company holds about 190 portal sign-ins of its own

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (company's own data)
trigger: Company must notify more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely for the company's own data. The customers with 1,000 or more affected individuals (for example a large store) carry this duty for theirs

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Affected individuals who reside outside Florida (customers in 5 other states; shoppers from anywhere)
deadline: Varies by state; many states also require a service provider that maintains data for another business to notify that business (check each statute)
notify: Customers as data owners; residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Always check. Apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside

trigger: Security incident affecting a customer's services or data
deadline: None today: the Terms of Service have no incident notice clause (P03 G-041). The update planned for 2026-12-31 adds one that matches the 10-day statutory clock
applies_at_this_tier: Gap - the statutory 10-day notice applies anyway

obligation: Stores' notice to their payment processors (context)
citation: Each store's merchant agreement with its processor (contract)
trigger: Suspected skimming of card data on a store's checkout page
applies_at_this_tier: No - the store's duty. The company tells each store promptly so it can meet its contract

citation: Upstream reseller terms (acceptable use and abuse handling)
trigger: Malware on sites hosted on the upstream platform
deadline: Not stated in the terms. Report in hours 1-2 so the provider does not suspend the whole reseller account
notify: Upstream provider abuse and support team

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom or extortion payment (for example a demand to stop leaking shopper data)
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
citation: FBI (IC3 online report); CISA incident reporting
trigger: Compromise of a tool that reaches many customers
deadline: As early as practical on day 1
Per policy terms; call before hiring outside firms
applies_at_this_tier: No policy today. A technology errors and omissions policy with a cyber endorsement was quoted; decision due 2026-12-31

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event report
trigger: Notification event involving the information of at least 500 consumers at a financial institution
deadline: As soon as possible, and no later than 30 days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is not a financial institution under the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act. If a customer is one, the customer reports its own event

trigger: Computer-security incident that materially disrupts or degrades, or is reasonably likely to, covered services to a bank for four or more hours
deadline: As soon as possible after the determination
notify: Bank-designated point of contact at each affected bank
applies_at_this_tier: No - no bank customers. Recheck if a bank becomes a customer

trigger: Cyber incident affecting covered defense information or a covered contractor information system
notify: DoD (DIBNet portal); subcontractors also notify the prime
applies_at_this_tier: No - no DoD contracts and no covered defense information

citation: FedRAMP Consolidated Rules for 2026: Incident Evaluation and Communication rules
trigger: A FedRAMP reportable incident affecting federal customer data
deadline: Per the FedRAMP rules for the certified offering
applies_at_this_tier: No - no federal customer and no FedRAMP certification. The company resells another provider's platform

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (C-IT-R06, pending final rule)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Statute: 72 hours (covered incident); 24 hours (ransom payment). Not yet effective
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck when final

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
